label: ESTIMATE
scope: Visa U.S. credit interchange for commercial cards, card-not-present B2B sale. Interchange only: excludes processor markup, assessments, and the participation fee some secondary sources report (0.05%). Not a claim of savings achieved; the Braintree sandbox never shows interchange charged.
how_it_was_read: Primary source: the Visa PDF was downloaded on 2026-11-07 and its text extracted with pypdf; rates below are copied from the extracted pages. Secondary sources were read as web pages and are used only to show where sources disagree.

sources.title: Visa USA Interchange Reimbursement Fees (Visa Supplemental Requirements)
sources.pages: printed p.16 (Corporate and Purchasing), p.21 (Business, excluding prepaid)

sources.title: Visa CEDP and Level 3 data: B2B interchange in 2026
sources.says: Commercial Product 3 1.75% + $0.10; Commercial Card Not Present 2.70% + $0.10; Non-Qualified 2.95% + $0.10; cites a Visa document dated 18 April 2026. Agrees with the Visa schedule.

sources.title: Visa CEDP Rates 2026: Product 3 Interchange Tables
sources.says: Corporate/Purchasing Product 3 (verified) 1.75% + $0.10; non-verified 2.05% + $0.10. Page dates are internally inconsistent and it does not reproduce Visa's schedule.
sources.conflict: Its 2.05% non-verified fallback conflicts with Visa's 24 Oct 2026 schedule (Card Not Present 2.70%, Non-Qualified 2.95%). Visa's Level 2 programme ended in April 2026, so this figure is likely out of date.

sources.title: It's Level 3 or bust as Visa's interchange shift rewires B2B data
sources.says: Visa ended its Level 2 interchange programme on 18 April 2026; interchange now depends on verified Level 3 data. Gives no rate figures.

sources.title: Visa's new Commercial Enhanced Data Program: what merchants need to know
sources.says: Merchants with errors or incomplete data 'could face a 40% increase'; gives a $500 example of about $9.60 (qualifying) versus up to $14.85 (downgraded) attributed to an external link, not to Visa.
sources.conflict: The $9.60 example implies about 1.90% + $0.10 for the qualifying case, versus Visa's 1.75% + $0.10 for Commercial Product 3. Older (Oct 2025) and not Visa data.

sources.title: What changed with Visa interchange fees in 2026?
sources.says: Small business Level 2 rates rose 75 bps on 24 Jan 2026 and Product 3 small business rates 65 bps. Not about corporate/purchasing cards.

rates.card_program: Visa Business, credit spend tier I
rates.note: Tiers II-V are 2.55 / 2.60 / 2.70 / 2.75 for Product 3 and 2.80 / 2.85 / 2.95 / 3.00 for Product 1: the gap is 0.25 points in every tier.

rates.card_program: Visa Business, credit spend tier I

scenarios.label: Visa Business card (standard Product 1 vs Product 3)
Visa Purchasing/Corporate card, downgraded to Non-Qualified

conflicts: The sandbox test card is only flagged 'Commercial: Yes'; its Visa product (Business vs Purchasing/Corporate) is unknown, so the estimate is a range across Visa's own schedule.

Verisave (Jan 2026) lists a 2.05% + $0.10 non-verified rate for Corporate/Purchasing; Visa's 24 Oct 2026 schedule has no such line (fallbacks are 2.70% and 2.95%). Not used in the range because it predates the April 2026 retirement of Level 2; its figure would give a smaller difference than the low end already shown.
Digital Transactions (Oct 2025) implies about 1.90% + $0.10 for qualifying Level 3; Visa's schedule says 1.75% + $0.10. Visa's figure is used.
Sources disagree on whether small-business cards benefit; this estimate is for corporate/purchasing/business cards only.
excluded: Processor markup (interchange-plus merchants only: blended-rate merchants will not see the difference)
Visa participation fee reported by secondary sources (0.05% on applicable enhanced-data transactions); not found in Visa's schedule text
Network assessments and any retroactive downgrade or clawback after Visa's data checks
